content.title: Identity Board | Environments Change, Identity Holds
content.summary: Keep a fixed identity board visible while the live environment changes. Each setting verifies the same subject through a different action, scale relationship, or camera role; this is an evidence variant of the existing identity-board template, not a new selector entry.

quick_start.input_format: Original subject + fixed character board + at least 4 environments + different verification actions/scales/camera movements in each location + final character board compared with the real scene
quick_start.recommended_input: The ceramic messenger is continuously compared with the fixed character board: he enters sequentially the packaging room, kiln, glaze laboratory, and rain-soaked loading/unloading area, demonstrating different actions and camera movements in each location, and finally completes the comparison with the same character board in the exhibition hall.
required_anchors: The character board maintains the same layout throughout
The same identity remains stable across at least four environments
Each environment has distinct verification responsibilities
The ending character board is readable simultaneously with the final scene
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A fixed character board remains visible while live-action environments, actions, scales, and camera positions change to verify one stable identity; this is a second evidence source for the existing identity-board template and does not add a new selector entry.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Keep one compact identity board visible as a persistent verification anchor while the live evidence field changes through several environments. Each new field must prove a different behavior, scale or camera relation of the same subject; return to a readable board-plus-live-image composition often enough that variety never outruns identity.

invariants.rule: Keep one compact identity board or reference panel readable across the sequence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without the anchor, the piece becomes an unrelated environment montage.

invariants.rule: Change the live evidence field at least three times while preserving one subject identity.
invariants.ablation_failure: Too little variation cannot prove transfer robustness.

invariants.rule: Give each environment a different proof role: action, scale, profile, close detail or interaction.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeating the same pose in new backgrounds adds no new evidence.

invariants.rule: Preserve face, silhouette and costume logic even when lighting and camera change.
invariants.ablation_failure: Identity drift defeats the verification task.

invariants.rule: End with both the stable anchor and one final live proof readable together.
invariants.ablation_failure: A decorative end card without live evidence cannot close the test.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.
